summary: Verified the requirements.txt dependency-conflict fix (bug #2 from the Windows installer). REAL clean install: python3 -m venv /tmp/reqtest-full + pip install -r /app/backend/requirements.txt => exit 0, NO ResolutionImpossible, 29 packages resolved (fastapi 0.141.1, starlette 1.6.0, pydantic 2.13.4/pydantic-core 2.46.4, motor 3.7.1 + pymongo 4.17.0, uvicorn 0.52.4, httpx 0.28.1, bcrypt 5.0.0, PyJWT 2.13.0, routeros-api 0.21.0, python-dotenv 1.2.3). Zero internal/Emergent packages and zero grpc/google packages pulled in transitively. Import check in the clean venv passed: fastapi, uvicorn, motor, pydantic, dotenv, bcrypt, httpx, jwt, routeros_api, EmailStr, plus bson (comes free via pymongo/motor). Cross-checked every import in /app/backend/*.py (grep of all import statements) against the 9-package list: fully covered, nothing missing, nothing extra. Deeper than requested: (a) imported the whole app (server.py -> auth, routes_admin, routes_portal, payments, db, mikrotik, seed) INSIDE the clean venv - OK; (b) actually ran the app with the clean venv (uvicorn on 127.0.0.1:8099): /api/health -> {'ok':true}, CORS preflight 200, admin login (agungsetiadi220@gmail.com) -> 200 with httpOnly cookie + access-control-allow-credentials:true + explicit origin, no errors/warnings in uvicorn log. So the trimmed requirements work not only for install but at runtime with the newest resolved versions. Windows wheels: pip download --only-binary=:all: --platform win_amd64 for py3.12 AND py3.13 => bcrypt-5.0.0-cp39-abi3-win_amd64.whl (abi3, covers 3.9+), pydantic_core-2.48.0-cp312/cp313-win_amd64.whl, uvicorn + httpx pure-python wheels. No source build needed on Windows for the pinned-free set. Forbidden-token grep (emergentintegrations|litellm|customer-assets|grpcio|google-api-core) on requirements.txt => empty. Regression: 37/37 pytest pass (tests/backend_test.py + tests/test_security_iter2.py), cleanup_iter2.py executed afterwards (4 synthetic QA users deleted, 3 login_attempts cleared, 0 remaining, all seeded hashes $2b$/len=60). Running backend still healthy on :8001.

minor.issue: No minimum Python version check. requirements.txt is now fully unpinned; on an old interpreter (e.g. Python 3.8/3.9) pip will happily resolve BACKWARDS to ancient fastapi/pydantic (possibly pydantic v1), the install will 'succeed', and the app will then crash at runtime with a confusing error. Recommend asserting python >= 3.10 (e.g. parse (python --version) and Fail with 'Install Python 3.11+ dari python.org') and/or adding a floor via python_requires-style guidance in the installer message.

No upper bounds at all. Today it resolves cleanly (fastapi 0.141.1 / starlette 1.6.0 / bcrypt 5.0.0), and the app was verified to actually RUN on that set, but a future breaking major (fastapi 1.x, pydantic 3.x, bcrypt 6.x) will silently reach new users' machines. Consider soft caps like fastapi>=0.115,<1.0, pydantic[email]>=2.9,<3, motor>=3.6,<4, bcrypt>=4.2,<6 to make installs reproducible over time.

Informational: the 'emergentintegrations / customer-assets' filter is now a no-op since requirements.txt is clean. Harmless to keep as a safety net, but it also silently drops any line containing those substrings - fine. Note Out-File -Encoding ascii will fail if anyone later adds a non-ASCII comment to requirements.txt.

Pre-existing, not from this fix, but relevant to the Windows/LAN installer scenario: a Secure+SameSite=None cookie is rejected by browsers on the non-secure origin http://<lan-ip>:3000, so the httpOnly cookie session will not persist for phone/LAN users. Not fatal today because the frontend also stores the token in localStorage and sends Authorization: Bearer (lib/api.js), but the cookie path is effectively dead on LAN HTTP.
Informational: motor is deprecated upstream in favour of PyMongo's native async API. Not urgent (motor 3.7.1 installs and runs fine), but a future migration item.

action_items: Optional hardening: add a Python >= 3.10 check to setup_windows.ps1 so a fully-unpinned requirements.txt cannot resolve backwards to pydantic v1 on an old interpreter.
Optional: add upper bounds (fastapi<1.0, pydantic<3, motor<4, bcrypt<6) for reproducible installs.
Carry-over from iteration_4 (still open, installer UX): keep the elevated PowerShell window open on Fail() and handle UAC decline instead of exit 0.

The original ResolutionImpossible is gone because grpcio-status / google-api-core are no longer present at all.

Verified beyond a dry-run: the app was imported AND served under the freshly created venv, and admin login + CORS + httpOnly cookie all behaved identically to the running environment - so the unpinned upgrade to fastapi 0.141/starlette 1.6/bcrypt 5.0 introduces no runtime break. auth.py uses only bcrypt.hashpw/gensalt/checkpw, which are stable in bcrypt 5.x (no passlib dependency, so the well-known passlib+bcrypt5 breakage does not apply).

Windows binary risk is nil: bcrypt ships an abi3 win_amd64 wheel and pydantic-core ships cp312/cp313 win_amd64 wheels; uvicorn[standard] extras (uvloop) are correctly skipped on Windows by their own markers, so no compiler is required.

rca_of_the_issue: Root cause of the user's failure: requirements.txt was a pip freeze of the Emergent dev container, containing 127 strictly pinned packages including google-api-core[grpc]==2.33.0 and grpcio-status==1.71.2 whose pinned grpcio ranges are mutually exclusive, so pip's resolver had no valid solution on the user's Python -> ResolutionImpossible. None of those packages are imported by the application. The fix (9 unpinned core packages derived from the actual import graph) removes the conflicting nodes entirely; confirmed by a real clean-venv install plus a live run of the app on the newly resolved versions.
